questionText: The size of the physical address space of a processor is $2^P$ bytes. The word length is $2^W$ bytes. The capacity of cache memory is $2^N$ bytes. The size of each cache block is $2^M$ words. For a $K$-way set-associative cache memory, the length (in number of bits) of the tag field is
explanation:
Step 1: Total Physical Address Bits
Size of physical address space = $2^P$ bytes
Physical Address bits = $P$

Step 2: Block Size and Offset Bits
Word length = $2^W$ bytes
Block size = $2^M \text{ words} = 2^M \times 2^W = 2^{M+W} \text{ bytes}$
Block offset bits = $M + W$

Step 3: Number of Sets and Set Index Bits
Cache capacity = $2^N$ bytes
Number of blocks in cache = $\frac{\text{Cache Capacity}}{\text{Block Size}} = \frac{2^N}{2^{M+W}} = 2^{N - M - W}$
Number of sets in $K$-way set-associative cache = $\frac{2^{N - M - W}}{K} = 2^{N - M - W - \log_2 K}$
Set Index bits = $N - M - W - \log_2 K$

Step 4: Tag Bits Calculation
Physical Address = Tag bits + Set Index bits + Block Offset bits
$P = \text{Tag} + (N - M - W - \log_2 K) + (M + W)$
$P = \text{Tag} + N - \log_2 K$
$\text{Tag} = P - N + \log_2 K$
